newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares extend losses on blue chip sales.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares extend losses on blue chip sales.

text.p: Shares of blue chip companies remained under selling pressure at the Nigerian stock market on Monday, forcing the all-share index down.
The index fell to 7933.63 from 7975.21 on Friday,
The exchange said it had corrected a computer error which last week showed the index rising while market capitalisation fell.
Traders said shareholders were still dumping blue chip stocks to cushion the effect of Nigeria's economic woes.
"There is a large volume of shares out there for which there are no buyers," one trader said. "Some people are even ready to sell at a discount."
Oil marketers African Petroleum and Agip each fell 50 kobo to 46.30 naira and 11.00 naira, respectively.
Total TOTL.LG fell 30 kobo to 53.30 naira and Unipetrol was also down 30 kobo at 60.00 naira.
Conglomerates PZ Industries and Lever Brothers were 20 kobo weaker at 21.80 naira and 21.60 naira, respectively.
West African Portland Cement Company (WAPCO) fell 50 kobo to 58.00 naira and Ashaka Cement slid 25 kobo to 12.00 naira.
Leading bank UBA was 50 kobo down at 12.00 naira.
Nigerian Bottling Company dropped 10 kobo from its Friday 46.90 naira close and Flour Mills ended 60 kobo cheaper at 14.50 naira.
However, a handful of small shares were up on improved corporate results.
Among these was Afribank, which finished five kobo higher at 4.12.
Prestige Assurance rose 10 kobo to 6.70 naira while Afprint climbed five kobo to 2.80 naira and Vono appreciated by three kobo to 3.15 naira.
Construction firm Julius Berger was ex-dividend at 9.50 naira, 30 kobo down.
